children.name: Bradypus variegitatus
children.description: Descriptive notes. Head-body 519 - 540 mm, tail 52 - 55 mm, ear 8 - 22 mm, hindfoot 85 - 180 mm; weight 3.7 - 6 kg. Adult Brown-throated Three-toed Sloths weigh less than they appear due to long and thick pelage. Males are slightly smaller (less than 10 %) than females. They are gray, with long, coarse hair, but hair is often covered with mutualistic algae (and other microbiota), causing it to have green tinge. The Brown-throated Three-toed Sloth has a dark orbital stripe over a lighter colored and browner face, giving the appearance of a mask. Males have dorsal speculum of shorter cream to orange colored hair, with dark stripe running vertically down the center of it. Contrasting dorsalstripe appears to become accentuated with age and is sometimes accompanied by black spots on either side. Males and females have small vestigial tails. Forelimbs and hindlimbs have three large and distinctive claws. The Brown-throated Three-toed Sloth has long forelimbs (370 - 450 mm) and relatively short hindlimbs (320 - 370 mm). Chromosomal complement is 2 n = 54 - 55 and FN = 56 - 58.

children.name: Bradypodion damaranum
children.description: The Knysna dwarf chameleon (Bradypodion damaranum) is a species of dwarf chameleon in the Bradypodion ("slow footed") genus that is endemic to South Africa. It is a forest dweller, found only in a limited range in the afromontane forests near Knysna, South Africa, and in certain surrounding areas.

children.name: Bradypodion dracomontanum
children.description: The Drakensberg dwarf chameleon (Bradypodion dracomontanum) occurs in the Drakensberg, South Africa, between the latitudes of 27°45′ and 29°15′. Bright green dwarf chameleons (emerald dwarf chameleon) found in the Drakensberg south of 29°15′ are now known to be more closely related to the Natal Midlands dwarf chameleon (Bradypodion thamnobates) and may yet be described as a separate species.

children.name: Bradypodion gutturale
children.description: The Robertson dwarf chameleon, also known as the Little Karoo dwarf chameleon, (Bradypodion gutturale) is a chameleon in the genus Bradypodion. It is found in the dry Fynbos and Renosterveld shrub vegetation, in the centre of the Western Cape province, South Africa.

children.name: Bradypodion kentanicum
children.description: The Kentani dwarf chameleon (Bradypodion kentanicum) occurs in coastal area of the Eastern Cape, South Africa.

children.name: Bradypodion melanocephalum
children.description: The black-headed dwarf chameleon (Bradypodion melanocephalum) is a lizard of the family Chamaeleonidae endemic to KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. It is also known as the KwaZulu dwarf chamaeleon and Durban dwarf chameleon.

children.name: Bradypodion nemorale
children.description: The Zululand dwarf chameleon (Bradypodion nemorale) is a species of lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae. It is also known as the Qudeni dwarf chameleon. It is endemic to South Africa.

children.name: Bradypodion ngomeense

children.name: Bradypodion occidentale

children.name: Bradypodion pumilum
children.description:
The Cape dwarf chameleon (Bradypodion pumilum) is a chameleon native to the South African province of the Western Cape, where it is restricted to the region around Cape Town.
As with most chameleons, its tongue is twice the length of its body and it can be shot out of its mouth using a special muscle in the jaw. This gives the chameleon the ability to catch insects some distance away.

children.name: Bradypodion setaroi
children.description: Setaro's dwarf chameleon (Bradypodion setaroi) is a species of lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Bradypodion taeniabronchum
children.description: Smith's dwarf chameleon (Bradypodion taeniabronchum), also known as the Elandsberg dwarf chameleon, is a species of lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae endemic to Fynbos in South Africa's Eastern Cape. As in several species of chameleons in the genus Bradypodion, the Smith's dwarf chameleon can use its color-changing ability to actively camouflage itself depending on the vision of the specific predator species (for example, bird or snake) by which it is being threatened.

children.name: Bradypodion thamnobates
children.description: The Natal Midlands dwarf chameleon (Bradypodion thamnobates) is a chameleon native to woodland habitat in the inland Midlands area of the South African province of KwaZulu-Natal.

children.description: The Iaraka River leaf chameleon (Brookesia vadoni), also commonly known as the mossy pygmy leaf chameleon, is a species of chameleon, a lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae. The species is endemic to Madagascar.

children.name: Brookesia valerieae
children.description: Brookesia valerieae is a species of chameleon, a lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Brookesia nana

children.name: Nadzikambia
children.description: Nadzikambia — a genus of chameleons in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Nadzikambia baylissi
children.description: The Mount Mabu chameleon (Nadzikambia baylissi) is one of two species in the genus Nadzikambia (derived from the species' name in Chichewa). It is a small chameleon from Mount Mabu in Mozambique.

children.name: Nadzikambia mlanjensis
children.description:
The Mlanje Mountain chameleon (Nadzikambia mlanjensis) is one of two species in the genus Nadzikambia (derived from the species' name in Chichewa). It is a plesiomorphic, small chameleon from the Ruo Gorge forest on Mount Mulanje in Malawi.
Initially placed into Chamaeleo, it was for some time moved to the South African dwarf chameleons (Bradypodion) by some. This was criticized because plesiomorphies cannot be used to define clades, and eventually turned out to be in error.

children.name: Nadzikambia natalensis
children.description: Characterisation: The monophyly of Nadzikambia is established on the basis of a suite of mitochondrial and nuclear genetic characters and a unique hemipenis. The latter is rather short and stout with a short pedicel and shallow calyces. There are no rotulae on the apex, which are replaced with a pair of large fleshy, papillate lobes with scalloped edges. At the sulcal base of each lobe are one or two pedunculated papillae (Klaver & Böhme 1986). The lungs show a structure similar to that of Kinyongia, with two pairs of long diverticulae trailing from the inferior and posterior surfaces of the lung. A series of four small septae alternate with five larger septae across the dorsal wall with several smaller septae arising from the ventral and cephalic walls. There is no gular pouch (Klaver 1977). The parietal peritoneum is unpigmented and reproduction oviparous. The external morphology is largely conservative, and gular and ventral crests are absent. There is a weak dorsal crest, finely heterogeneous scalation that forms rosettes of tubercles on the lower flanks, and a low casque. Although cranial morphology remains undescribed, the external appearance of the cranial crests suggest that the cranium is constructed in the same manner as Kinyongia.

children.name: Kinyongia
children.description: Kinyongia — a genus of chameleons in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Kinyongia adolfifriderici
children.description: Kinyongia adolfifriderici is a species of chameleon, a lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Kinyongia asheorum
children.description: Kinyongia asheorum, also known commonly as the Mount Nyiro bearded chameleon, is a species of lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Kinyongia boehmei
children.description: Kinyongia boehmei, the Taita blade-horned chameleon, Böhme's two-horned chameleon and Dwarf fischer's chameleon, is species of chameleon, a lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae, found only in the Taita Hills of southeastern Kenya.

children.name: Kinyongia carpenteri
children.description: Kinyongia carpenteri, commonly called Carpenter's chameleon or the helmeted chameleon, is a species of chameleon, a lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Kinyongia excubitor
children.description: Mount Kenya sentinel chameleon, or Mount Kenya hornless chameleon (Kinyongia excubitor), is a species of chameleons endemic to Kenya. It is known from Mount Kenya, Nyambeni Hills, and Aberdare Range.

children.name: Kinyongia fischeri
children.description: Fischer's chameleon (Kinyongia fischeri), also known commonly as the Nguru blade-horned chameleon and the Nguru two-horned chameleon, is a species of chameleon, a lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae. The species is endemic to Tanzania.

children.name: Kinyongia gyrolepis
children.description: Kinyongia gyrolepis is a species of Kinyongia chameleons first described in 2012, and the sister species to the Kinyongia adolfifriderici chameleon.

children.name: Kinyongia itombwensis
children.description: Kinyongia itombwensis is a species of chameleons endemic to the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.

children.name: Kinyongia magomberae
children.description: Kinyongia magomberae, the Magombera chameleon or Magombera single-horned chameleon, is an endangered species of chameleon found only in humid submontane forests in the Udzungwa Mountains in Tanzania.

children.name: Kinyongia matschiei
children.description: Kinyongia matschiei, common name giant monkey-tailed east Usambara two-horned chameleon, giant east Usambara blade-horned chameleon, and Matschie's two-horned chameleon, is a species of chameleon from the East Usambara Mountains in Tanzania.

children.name: Kinyongia msuyae
children.description: Kinyongia msuyae is a species of chameleons endemic to the Udzungwa Mountain region in Tanzania.

children.name: Kinyongia multituberculata
children.description: The West Usambara two-horned chameleon or West Usambara blade-horned chameleon (Kinyongia multituberculata) is a species of chameleon endemic to the West Usambara Mountains of Tanzania. Until 2008, it was generally confused with Fischer's chameleon (K. Fischeri), which is not found in the Usambara Mountains. None of its close relatives occur in the same range as K. Multituberculata, but K. Matschiei and K. Vosseleri are restricted to the East Usambaras.

children.name: Kinyongia mulyai
children.description: Kinyongia mulyai is a species of chameleons first described in 2015, endemic to the Nzawa forest regions of the south-eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.

children.name: Kinyongia oxyrhina
children.description:
The sharp-nosed chameleon (Kinyongia oxyrhina) is a chameleon native to the Uluguru and Udzungwa Mountains of Tanzania, where it inhabits forests (also secondary), woodlands and plantations at an altitude of above sea level.
It reached up to in total length, with about half being the tail. Adult males have a distinct soft and blade-like horn on the nose where the tip is movable; females lack a horn. Its colours are very variable, but typically shades of brown, grey, green or rusty-red, and especially during the mating season may have some blue patches.

children.name: Kinyongia tavetana
children.description: Kinyongia tavetana, the Kilimanjaro two-horned chameleon or Kilimanjaro blade-horned chameleon, is a species of chameleon in the genus Kinyongia.

children.name: Kinyongia tenuis
children.description: Kinyongia tenuis, also known as the Usambara soft-horned chameleon, Usambara flap-nosed chameleon and Matschie's dwarf chameleon, is a fairly small species of chameleon from Kenya and Tanzania.

children.name: Kinyongia uluguruensis
children.description: Kinyongia uluguruensis is a species of chameleon, also known as the Uluguru two-horned chameleon or Uluguru two-horned chamaeleon.

children.name: Kinyongia uthmoelleri
children.description: Kinyongia uthmoelleri, known commonly as the Hanang hornless chameleon, Müller's leaf chameleon, and Uthmöller's chameleon, is species of lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Kinyongia vanheygeni
children.description: Kinyongia vanheygeni, the Poroto single-horned chameleon or Van Heygen's chameleon, is a species of chameleon, a lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Kinyongia vosseleri
children.description: Kinyongia vosseleri, also known commonly as the Usambara two-horned chameleon and Vosseler's blade-horned chameleon, is an endangered species of lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Kinyongia xenorhina
children.description:
The strange-horned chameleon (Kinyongia xenorhina), also known as Rwenzori plate-nosed chameleon or single welded-horn chameleon, is a species of chameleon. It is native to the rainforests of the Ruwenzori Mountains of western Uganda and eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.
The strange-horned chameleon is named for the large protuberance extending from the top of its snout, particularly prominent on the males of the species. This feature is composed of two separate plates extending outwards from either side of the snout and merging at the end. This feature has also earned it the alternate common name single welded-horn chameleon. It also has a very high casque (a helmet-like structure towards the back of the skull). The head and casque are covered with enlarged, plate-like scales.

children.name: Furcifer
children.description: Furcifer — a genus of chameleons in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Furcifer angeli
children.description: The Angel's chameleon (Furcifer angeli), initially described as Chamaeleo angeli, is a species of chameleon, a lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae. The species is endemic to Madagascar, and was originally described by Édouard-Raoul Brygoo and Charles Antoine Domergue in 1968.

children.name: Furcifer antimena
children.description: The Antimena chameleon (Furcifer antimena) is a species of chameleon that is endemic to southwest Madagascar.

children.name: Furcifer balteatus
children.description: Furcifer balteatus, also known as the two-banded chameleon or the rainforest chameleon, is a species of chameleon that is endemic to Madagascar. It was described by André Marie Constant Duméril and Gabriel Bibron in 1851.

children.name: Furcifer belalandaensis
children.description: Furcifer belalandaensis, also commonly known as the Belalanda chameleon or the Sangoritan'i Belalanda, is a species of chameleon that is endemic to Madagascar.

children.name: Furcifer bifidus
children.description: Furcifer bifidus, also known as the fork-nosed chameleon, is a species of chameleon that is endemic to Madagascar.

children.name: Furcifer campani
children.description: The jewelled chameleon (Furcifer campani), also commonly known as Campan's chameleon or the Madagascar forest chameleon, is a species of lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Furcifer cephalolepis
children.description: Furcifer cephalolepis is a species of chameleon that is endemic to Grande Comore.

children.name: Furcifer labordi
children.description: Labord's chameleon (Furcifer labordi) is a species of chameleon, a lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae. The species is endemic to dry and deciduous forests, including spiny forests, in lowlands of western Madagascar, at altitudes. It is considered vulnerable because of ongoing habitat loss.

children.name: Furcifer lateralis
children.description: The carpet chameleon (Furcifer lateralis), also known as the jewel chameleon or white-lined chameleon, is a species of chameleon that is endemic to eastern Madagascar.

children.name: Furcifer major
children.description: Furcifer major, the southern carpet chameleon, is a species of chameleon found in various dry habitats of southern Madagascar.

children.name: Furcifer minor
children.description: The lesser chameleon (Furcifer minor) or minor chameleon is a species of lizards in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Furcifer monoceras
children.description: The long-nosed rhinoceros chameleon (Furcifer monoceras) is a species of chameleon endemic to Madagascar.

children.name: Furcifer nicosiai
children.description: Furcifer nicosiai is a large species of chameleon, a lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Furcifer oustaleti
children.description: The Malagasy giant chameleon (Furcifer oustaleti), also known commonly as Oustalet's chameleon, is a large species of chameleon which is native to the entirety of Madagascar, but also has been introduced near Nairobi in Kenya (though its current status there is unclear) and in Miami-Dade County in the United States. It occurs in a wide range of habitats, even among degraded vegetation within villages, but is relatively rare in the interior of primary forest.

children.name: Furcifer pardalis
children.description: The panther chameleon (Furcifer pardalis) is a species of chameleon found in the eastern and northern parts of Madagascar in a tropical forest biome.

children.name: Furcifer petteri
children.description: The Petter's chameleon (Furcifer petteri) is a species of chameleon, which is endemic to northern Madagascar. Furcifer petteri was initially described as the subspecies Chamaeleo willsii petteri by Édouard-Raoul Brygoo and Charles Domergue in 1966, but later transferred to the genus Furcifer and given full species status by Frank Glaw and Miguel Vences in 1994.

children.name: Furcifer polleni
children.description: The Mayotte chameleon (Furcifer polleni) is a species of chameleon that is endemic to Mayotte in the Comoros Islands.

children.name: Furcifer rhinoceratus
children.description: The rhinoceros chameleon (Furcifer rhinoceratus) is a species of chameleon that gets its common name from its horn-like nose which is most prominent in males.

children.name: Furcifer timoni
children.description: Furcifer timoni is a species of chameleon, a lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Furcifer tuzetae
children.description: Furcifer tuzetae is a species of chameleon that is endemic to Madagascar.

children.name: Furcifer verrucosus
children.description: Furcifer verrucosus, also known as the warty chameleon, spiny chameleon or crocodile chameleon, is a species of reptile endemic to Madagascar.

children.name: Furcifer viridis
children.description: Furcifer viridis, the green chameleon, is a species of chameleon found widely in forest, scrub and grasslands in western and northern Madagascar.

children.name: Furcifer willsii
children.description: The canopy chameleon (Furcifer willsii), also known commonly as Wills's chameleon or incorrectly as Will's chameleon, is a species of lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Trioceros
children.description: Trioceros — a genus of chameleons in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Trioceros affinis
children.description: Trioceros affinis, Rüppell's desert chameleon or beardless Ethiopian montane chameleon, is a species of chameleon endemic to Ethiopia.

children.name: Trioceros balebicornutus
children.description: Trioceros balebicornutus, the Bale two-horned chameleon, is a species of chameleon.

children.name: Trioceros bitaeniatus
children.description:
The side-striped chameleon or the two-lined chameleon (Trioceros bitaeniatus) is a chameleon native to Ethiopia, southern Sudan, Somalia, Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, and the northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.
In Kenya, the side-striped chameleon lives on Mount Kenya, Kilimanjaro, and in the Aberdare Range. They live in the Hagenia and Hypericum scrub in the timberline forest between 3000 and 4000 m. It lives between above the ground in the giant heathers that grow here. They are strictly diurnal and shelter at night between dense bushes.

children.name: Trioceros camerunensis
children.description: Trioceros camerunensis, the Cameroon dwarf chameleon, is a species of chameleon endemic to Cameroon.

children.name: Trioceros chapini
children.description: Trioceros chapini, also known commonly as Chapin's chameleon, the gray chameleon, and the grey chameleon, is a species of lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Trioceros conirostratus
children.description: Trioceros conirostratus, the South Sudanese unicorn chameleon, is a species of chameleon found in South Sudan and Uganda.

children.name: Trioceros cristatus
children.description: The crested chameleon (Trioceros cristatus), also known as the sail backed chameleon, is a species of chameleon native to forests and semi-open wooded habitats in Central Africa.

children.name: Trioceros deremensis
children.description: Trioceros deremensis, the Usambara three-horned chameleon or wavy chameleon, is a species of chameleon that is endemic to forests in the Eastern Arc Mountains of Tanzania.

children.name: Trioceros ellioti
children.description: Trioceros ellioti, also known commonly as Elliot's chameleon, Elliot's groove-throated chameleon, and the montane side-striped chameleon, is a species of lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Trioceros feae
children.description: Trioceros feae, also known commonly as the Bioko montane chameleon and Fea's chameleon, is a species of lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Trioceros fuelleborni
children.description: Trioceros fuelleborni, also known commonly as the flapjack chameleon, the Ngosi Volcano chameleon, and the Poroto three-horned chameleon, is a species of lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Trioceros goetzei
children.description: Trioceros goetzei, also known commonly as Goetze's chameleon, Goetze's whistling chameleon, and the Ilolo chameleon, is a species of lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Trioceros hanangensis
children.description: Trioceros hanangensis, the Mount Hanang dwarf chameleon or Mount Hanang chameleon, is a species of chameleon found in Tanzania.

children.name: Trioceros harennae
children.description: Trioceros harennae, also known commonly as the Harenna hornless chameleon, is a species of lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Trioceros hoehnelii
children.description: Trioceros hoehnelii, commonly known as von Höhnel's chameleon, the helmeted chameleon, and the high-casqued chameleon, is a species of chameleon, a lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Trioceros incornutus
children.description: Trioceros incornutus, the Ukinga hornless chameleon, is a species of chameleon found in Tanzania.

children.name: Trioceros ituriensis
children.description: Trioceros ituriensis, the Ituri forest chameleon, is a species of chameleon found in Democratic Republic of the Congo and Kenya.

children.name: Trioceros jacksonii
children.description: Jackson's chameleon (Trioceros jacksonii), also known commonly as Jackson's horned chameleon, the three-horned chameleon, and the Kikuyu three-horned chameleon, is a species of chameleon, a lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae. The species is native to East Africa, and introduced to Hawaii, Florida, and California. There are three recognized subspecies.

children.name: Trioceros johnstoni
children.description: Trioceros johnstoni, known commonly as Johnston's chameleon, Johnston's three-horned chameleon, and the Ruwenzori three-horned chameleon, is a species of chameleon, a lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Trioceros kinangopensis
children.description: Trioceros kinangopensis, the Aberdare Mountains dwarf chameleon, is a species of chameleon found in Kenya.

children.name: Trioceros kinetensis
children.description: Trioceros kinetensis, or the Mount Kineti chameleon, is a species of chameleon found in South Sudan.

children.name: Trioceros laterispinis
children.description: The spiny-flanked chameleon (Trioceros laterispinis), also known as the spiny-sided chameleon, is a species of chameleon endemic to Tanzania. It was first described in 1932 by Arthur Loveridge.

children.name: Trioceros marsabitensis
children.description: Trioceros marsabitensis, Tilbury's chameleon, Mount Marsabit chameleon, or Mount Marsabit one-horned chameleon, is a species of chameleon endemic to Kenya.

children.name: Trioceros melleri
children.description: Meller's chameleon (Trioceros melleri), also known commonly as the giant one-horned chameleon, is a species of lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae. Meller's chameleon is the largest species of chameleon from the African mainland, i.e., the largest of the chameleons not native to Madagascar.

children.name: Trioceros montium
children.description: The Cameroon sailfin chameleon or Cameroon two-horned mountain chameleon (Trioceros montium) is a species of chameleon endemic to Cameroon. It has a very unusual appearance.

children.name: Trioceros narraioca
children.description: Trioceros narraioca, the Mount Kulal chameleon or Mount Kulal stump-nosed chameleon, is a species of chameleon endemic to Kenya.

children.name: Trioceros ntunte
children.description: Trioceros ntunte, the Mount Nyiru chameleon or Nyiru montane chameleon, is a species of chameleon endemic to Kenya.

children.name: Trioceros nyirit
children.description: Trioceros nyirit, the Mount Mtelo stump-nosed chameleon or Pokot chameleon, is a species of chameleon endemic to Kenya.

children.name: Trioceros oweni
children.description: Owen's chameleon (Trioceros oweni), also commonly known as Owen's three-horned chameleon, is a species of lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae. The species is native to forests in central Africa. Named after British naval officer and explorer William Fitzwilliam Owen, it was first described in 1831 by the naturalist John Edward Gray, and is the type species of the genus Trioceros.

children.name: Trioceros perreti
children.description: Trioceros perreti, Perret's chameleon or Perret's montane chameleon, is a species of chameleon found in Cameroon.

children.name: Trioceros pfefferi
children.description: Trioceros pfefferi, Pfeffer's chameleon or the Bakossi two-horned chameleon, is a species of chameleon endemic to Cameroon.

children.name: Trioceros quadricornis
children.description: The four-horned chameleon (Trioceros quadricornis) is a species of chameleon, a lizard in the family Chamaeleonidae. The species is native to highland areas in western Cameroon and southeastern Nigeria.

children.name: Trioceros rudis
children.description: The coarse chameleon (Trioceros rudis), also known as the rudis chameleon, Ruwenzori side-striped chameleon or the Rwenzori bearded chameleon, Contrary to common belief, this species does not inhabit Mount Meru, Tanzania.

children.name: Trioceros schoutedeni
children.description: Trioceros schoutedeni, Schouteden's montane dwarf chameleon, is a species of chameleon found in Rwanda and Democratic Republic of the Congo.

children.name: Trioceros schubotzi
children.description: Trioceros schubotzi, the Mt.

children.name: Trioceros serratus
children.description: Trioceros serratus is a species of chameleon found in Cameroon.

children.name: Trioceros sternfeldi
children.description: Trioceros sternfeldi, the Crater Highlands side-striped chameleon or Tanzanian montane dwarf chameleon, is a species of chameleon found in Tanzania.

children.name: Trioceros tempeli
children.description: Trioceros tempeli, the Tanzania mountain chameleon or Udzungwa double-bearded chameleon, is a species of chameleon endemic to Tanzania.

children.name: Trioceros werneri
children.description: Trioceros werneri, the Wemer's chameleon or Wemer's three-horned chameleon, is a species of chameleon that is endemic to forests and nearby gardens at altitudes of in the Eastern Arc Mountains of Tanzania.

children.name: Trioceros wiedersheimi
children.description: Trioceros wiedersheimi, the Mount Lefo chameleon or Wiedersheim's montane chameleon, is a species of chameleon found in Cameroon and Nigeria.

children.name: Archaius
children.description: Archaius — a genus of chameleons in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Archaius tigris
children.description: The tiger chameleon (Archaius tigris), (from Greek αρχαίος, meaning "ancient", archaic) also known as the Seychelles tiger chameleon, is the only species in the resurrected genus Archaius.

children.name: Palleon
children.description: Palleon — a genus of chameleons in the family Chamaeleonidae.

children.name: Palleon nasus
children.description: Palleon nasus, commonly known as the elongate leaf chameleon, is a species of chameleon endemic to Madagascar.
